description: 1100 Yarbrough is a 6 lane, two way roadway divided by an unprotected median that travels northbound and southbound. 10500 Vista Del Sol is a 4 lane, two way roadway divided by a two way left turn lane that travels eastbound and westbound. Unit 2 was traveling northbound on the inside lane of 1100 Yarbrough. Unit 1 was traveling southbound on the middle lane of 1200 Yarbrough. Unit 2 had a green light at the intersection of Yarbrough and Vista Del Sol and continued straight into the intersection. Unit 1 turned eastbound onto Vista Del Sol from the middle lane where a left turn is not permitted. Unit 1 and Unit 2 collided at the intersection. The driver of Unit 1 was transported by Fire Medical Services to Del Sol Medical Center due to a small laceration on his forehead. The driver of Unit 2 was not injured. The driver of Unit 1 was not cited due to the fact that he was receiving medical treatment for the laceration on his forehead. There were no reported witnesses.

1200 N. Yarbrough at the point of the collision has 4 lanes going northbound and 4 southbound, with a mandatory left-turn lane in each direction. 10600 Vista Del Sol is a 6-lane/2-way roadway that runs east and westbound. Driver-1 from Unit 1 stated she was traveling north on the 1100 block of Yarbrough in the center lane as she came into the intersection. Driver-1 stated she didn't recall if the traffic signal was green or red. She stated that she only remembered the impact which caused Unit 1 to spin and impact a light pole. Unit 2, Driver 2 stated he was traveling west on Vista Del Sol in the center lane as he approached the intersection. Driver-2 stated he had a green light and proceeded through the intersection. Driver-2 said that he abruptly saw Unit-1 cross his lane of travel and was unable to avoid a collision. As a result, Unit-2's front end struck Unit-1's right panel, causing her to spin out of control. Unit-1's left back quarter panel then collided with the signal light pole, which broke off its base and fell on the roof of Unit-3. Officer spoke with Driver-3 of Unit-3, who could not recall the chain of events. Driver-3 stated that he only recalled stopping at the intersection and feeling the impact of the signal light on the roof of his vehicle. Officer then spoke with the witness. The witness stated he was stationary in the left-turn lane facing east on Vista Del Sol when Unit 1 failed to come to a complete stop and ran the red light. The witness stated that he observed Unit 2's front end strike Unit 1's right panel, causing Unit 1 to spin 180 degrees. The momentum caused Unit-1's back left quarter panel to collide with the signal light pole, knocking it over onto Unit 3. It is Officer's investigative opinion that Driver-1 was at fault for causing the collision by committing a red light violation. The driver from Unit 1 was cited for the violation. None of the drivers or occupants complained of any injuries at the scene, and there were no witness.
